description: The enforcement ladder for human-ruled glossary terms. A ruling in the decisions file already travels three ways: it is injected into every translation prompt's glossary, it is checked at the end by the instruction_compliance detector, and until now nothing stood between those two -- a model that declined the injected rendering shipped its own and the finding went to a report nobody acted on. This config bounds the one step of the ladder that costs money. The ladder itself: (1) injection, unchanged; (2) a per-unit check after translation -- a unit whose frozen source carries a ruled term's source as a normalized substring and whose target lacks the ruled rendering is a violation; (3) a violating unit whose target carries a known variant of the ruling (the auto glossary target the ruling displaced, recorded as dropped_from_auto, or the ruled source itself still standing untranslated) has that variant replaced by the ruled rendering deterministically, no model involved; (4) a violation with no known variant earns one retranslation whose instruction pins the ruled rendering; (5) what still violates is escalated -- the detector finding stands and the violation list travels with the finished document. term_enforce_retry_budget bounds level 4 per publication: how many pinned retranslations one run may buy. The conservation equation ruled == applied + variant_substituted + retried_ok + escalated is asserted into the report, so every ruled occurrence ends in exactly one named bucket.
